# spyro auth

Manage stored credentials (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service).

## Before you run it

Passwords live only in the OS keychain (service `spyro-cli`), never in spyro.toml. Non-interactive runs use `SPYRO_PASSWORD` or `SPYRO_PASSWORD_<PROFILE>` (upper-case) instead.

Read `spyro profiles` first for hosts and `remote_path`; the `spyro` skill has the safety rules.

## Reference (from `--help`)

### `spyro auth`

```text
Usage: spyro auth [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  Manage stored credentials (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service).

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  delete  Remove stored credentials from the OS keychain.
  list    Show which credentials are stored in the keychain.
  set     Store a credential in the OS keychain.
```

### `spyro auth delete`

```text
Usage: spyro auth delete [OPTIONS]

  Remove stored credentials from the OS keychain.

Options:
  -p, --profile TEXT  Profile name  [required]
  --help              Show this message and exit.
```

### `spyro auth list`

```text
Usage: spyro auth list [OPTIONS]

  Show which credentials are stored in the keychain.

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

### `spyro auth set`

```text
Usage: spyro auth set [OPTIONS]

  Store a credential in the OS keychain.

  One password per profile — used for both SSH and sudo. If --password is omitted, you'll be
  prompted securely (no echo).

Options:
  -p, --profile TEXT   Profile name  [required]
  -w, --password TEXT  Password (omit to prompt)
  -f, --force          Overwrite without prompting
  --help               Show this message and exit.
```
